title: What do the sum and the take away leave when divided by five?
description: Seventeen and twenty four are shown as full rows of five with loose dots. The rows add or take away, and the loose dots add or take away, which gives each remainder without working out the sum or the take away. Keeko's doubt is that the loose dots, six, are the remainder.
teaching_notes: One idea: write each number as full rows plus a remainder, then add or take away the rows and the remainders separately. Watch for students who stop at six loose dots when six is more than a full row of five.

source: 17 leaves remainder 2 and 24 leaves remainder 4 on division
video_script.why: The student sees that remainders add and take away like the numbers do, so the remainder of a sum or a take away can be found without working it out.
video_script.substitution: Seventeen and twenty four on division by five, with remainders two and four.
video_script.anchor: dots laid in rows of five, with the loose dots beside the full rows, as in the book's pictures of remainders
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the loose dots two and four and stops at six, but six dots make one more full row of five with one dot left.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum leaves remainder one and the take away leaves remainder two

final_answer.spoken: remainder one for the sum and remainder two for the take away

maths_rules: take away: rows 4 - 3 = 1, loose 4 - 2 = 2, so 24 - 17 = 5 x 1 + 2
video_script.design: Two piles of dots in rows of five. The rows go together, the loose dots go together, and extra loose dots make one more row.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book, What Remains; two piles of dots in rows of five, one pile with two loose dots, the other with four loose dots

marks.piles: the two piles of dots appear in rows of five with their loose dots
marks.ask: the words sum and take away appear between the piles

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is an idea from your book, in the part called What Remains.
<bookmark mark='piles'/>One number leaves remainder two on division by five, and another leaves remainder four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Without working out the sum or the take away, what remainder does each one leave?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 17 dots as 3 full rows of five and 2 loose; 24 dots as 4 full rows of five and 4 loose

marks.first: seventeen dots fall into three full rows with two loose dots
marks.second: twenty four dots fall into four full rows with four loose dots

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Seventeen dots make three full rows of five, with two dots loose.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Twenty four dots make four full rows of five, with four dots loose.
The loose dots are the remainder.

beats.on_screen: Given: 17 leaves remainder 2 and 24 leaves remainder 4 on division by 5

marks.given: the two numbers and their remainders are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, seventeen leaves remainder two and twenty four leaves remainder four on division by five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the remainders of 17 + 24 and 24 - 17 on division by 5, without working out the sum or the take away

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remainders of the sum and of the take away, without working them out.

marks.write: each number is written as five times its rows plus its remainder
marks.both: the two numbers are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write each number as five times its full rows, plus its remainder.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Seventeen is five times three plus two, and twenty four is five times four plus four.

marks.rows: the rows join: three rows and four rows make seven rows
marks.loose: the loose dots join: two and four make six
marks.regroup: five of the six loose dots form one more row, with one dot left

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step two, for the sum, add the full rows. Three rows and four rows make seven rows.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>Add the loose dots. Two and four make six.
<bookmark mark='regroup'/>Six loose dots fill one more row of five, with one dot left.
That makes eight rows and one over.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: take away: rows 4 - 3 = 1; loose dots 4 - 2 = 2; so 24 - 17 = 5 x 1 + 2

marks.rows: three rows are taken from four rows, leaving one row
marks.loose: two loose dots are taken from four, leaving two
marks.result: one row and two loose dots stay on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step three, for the take away, take the full rows from the full rows. Four rows take away three rows leaves one row.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>Take the loose dots from the loose dots. Four take away two leaves two.
<bookmark mark='result'/>One row and two dots are left.

marks.sum: forty one is split into eight rows of five and one over
marks.take: seven is split into one row of five and two over

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step four, check by working them out. Seventeen plus twenty four is forty one, which is five times eight plus one.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Twenty four take away seventeen is seven, which is five times one plus two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum leaves remainder one and the take away leaves remainder two.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the dots
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 2 + 4 = 6 loose dots; five of the six dots form one more row; one dot stays loose

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the six loose dots
marks.row: five of the six loose dots form a new row
marks.fix: one loose dot stays and is lit

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the remainder is six, because two loose dots and four loose dots make six.
<bookmark mark='row'/>But six loose dots are enough to fill one more row of five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Only one dot stays loose, and a remainder on division by five must be less than five.
